sentences.text: Airline Operations Centre integration provides the operational bridge between carrier recovery planning and the Meridian Regional Air Traffic Flow Management and Airport Collaborative Decision-Making System.
The Airline Operations Coordinator is known as Saffron in airline integration working sessions.
Each airline operations centre submits a Flight Intent Message through the Airline Interface Adapter using an authenticated system account managed by the Identity Access Service.

The Flight Intent Message includes the preferred route, requested departure timing, aircraft registration, turnaround status, crew readiness, and passenger connection sensitivity needed for flow assessment.
The Airline Interface Adapter validates message structure, maps carrier codes to the Business Rules Registry, and forwards accepted intent data to the Flight Data Exchange.
Invalid or incomplete intent submissions are rejected with machine-readable reasons so the Airline Operations Coordinator can correct them without informal voice coordination.
Accepted intents are reflected on the Common Situation Display as proposed airline actions until the Regional Flow Platform reconciles them with airport and airspace constraints.
The Demand Prediction Service uses current airline intents to refine departure demand, arrival demand, and recovery demand by time band.
The Capacity Assessment Module compares that demand with the Airport Capacity Plan and the current Airport Acceptance Rate before recommending operating limits.
The Capacity Assessment Module uses the Storm Cell Snapshot to qualify capacity confidence during convective weather impacts.
The Slot Allocation Engine converts accepted constraints into Calculated Takeoff Time values and Target Off Block Time guidance for affected flights.
Airline operations centres receive those constraints through the Airline Interface Adapter and may also view them in the Airport CDM Portal.
When a Ground Delay Program is active, the Slot Coordinator reviews airline requests for priority handling against published equity and operational feasibility rules.
Copperfin confirms airline recovery priorities before the Slot Allocation Engine publishes a revised constraint set.
The Airline Operations Coordinator evaluates each constraint against crew legality, aircraft rotation continuity, maintenance positioning, and passenger recovery commitments.
If the airline proposes a retime, cancellation, aircraft substitution, or route change, it submits an updated Flight Intent Message rather than relying on manual annotations.
The Ground Handling Dispatcher sends the Crew Bus Delay Slip when crew transport lateness affects an aircraft turn.
Ground handling impacts are correlated by the Handling Resource Planner with stand occupancy, baggage readiness, catering status, and boarding progress.
The Ramp Control Lead uses the Ramp Movement Board to identify whether the proposed recovery action can be supported without creating surface congestion.
The Tower Supervisor reviews metering effects in the Tower Sequence Manager when airline recovery actions change the expected departure order.
The Airport Duty Manager monitors the Common Situation Display to ensure airline recovery decisions remain consistent with terminal capacity and passenger processing conditions.
Disputed constraints are captured in the Collaborative Decision Log with the requesting airline, operational rationale, decision owner, and final resolution.

During Adverse Weather Mode or a Capacity Reduction State, airline operations centres are expected to submit conservative intents that distinguish firm operating plans from speculative recovery options.
During the Recovery Phase, the Regional Flow Platform permits more frequent intent updates while retaining the previous values needed for audit and performance review.
The Performance Analytics Warehouse later compares submitted intents, issued constraints, actual off-block times, and achieved arrival outcomes to improve recovery playbooks.
All airline integration transactions are time-stamped by the Time Synchronization Service and preserved in the Audit Event Ledger for post-operations reconstruction.
